review_scope: Source and proposal only. No build, browser, workflow, UI, account, permission, role, fixture execution, or product/inventory changes.

verdict_a_procedure_adequacy.overall: PARTIAL: prior role-isolation and downloaded-file cleanup findings are addressed; history and recently-closed fixture setup remains too vague for reproducible owned-fixture assertions.

prior_findings.separate_role_profiles_and_fixtures: ADDRESSED — each case calls for a role-specific dedicated disposable profile, and shared_role_lifecycle prohibits cross-role reuse of profile, fixture, session ID, or download record.
prior_findings.downloaded_file_cleanup_outside_profile: ADDRESSED — exact owned path is recorded, only that file is removed and checked absent, and uncertainty is reported if path/absence cannot be confirmed; profile retirement is explicitly insufficient evidence.

cases.EXT-F-4042-T01: PARTIAL — handler/schema and assertions align, but 'prepare shared history fixture' does not specify the owned URLs/titles to visit or the exact visit steps; cannot reproduce the two expected rows from this procedure alone.
cases.EXT-F-4043-T01: ADEQUATE AS SOURCE-DERIVED PROCEDURE — names the committed synthetic fixture, link, filename, completion precondition, query/filter and malformed state. Browser completion remains unverified.
cases.EXT-F-4094-T01: PARTIAL — schema and sessions preflight align, but setup does not name the exact disposable page/title to open and close to create the expected session row.
cases.EXT-F-4165-T01: PARTIAL — canonical action/schema paths align, but it inherits the underspecified history fixtures from EXT-F-4042; distinctive hostname and URLs are not concretely provisioned.
cases.EXT-F-4166-T01: PARTIAL — list/restore flow safely uses only the ID returned for the controlled fixture and avoids omitted-ID restore; the exact fixture page/title/tab creation and closure steps remain unspecified.

remaining_procedure_findings: No checked-in history/session fixture is identified by this proposal. Define concrete owned URLs and expected titles, exact page-opening steps per role, and which single test tab to close; keep fixture values distinct or otherwise isolated across roles.

Per-case cleanup sentences can read as deleting each role's profile after each case, while shared_role_lifecycle says run all cases for a role and then clean up. Clarify that cleanup occurs once after that role's full case set, preserving its profile between applicable cases.

verdict_b_safety_quality_false_coverage.overall: PASS WITH PROCEDURE CLARITY GAPS: no new false runtime or authorization claim found; schema negatives, reachability boundary, and cleanup language are materially improved.
findings: ToolsView.tsx manual Run parses and safe-parses handler arguments, then invokes handler.run directly with permissionMode='act'; procedures correctly state this does not exercise dispatcher Ask/Act authorization or prove live tool binding.

Malformed cases match Zod schemas and are rejected before handler execution: minutes=0 (list_recent_history), state='paused' (list_downloads), max_results=0 (list_recently_closed), action='other' (chrome_history and chrome_recently_closed). These are argument-validation negatives only.

Chrome sessions is required in the Chrome manifest permissions and is absent from optional_permissions; sessions handler metadata requests it as an optional permission, but the proposal correctly treats loaded-artifact preflight as required and does not propose toggling/removing it or call absence an authorization denial.
The source fixture is synthetic and self-contained. Proposal accurately leaves completed download, loaded artifact, session retention/restore, both role runs, and cleanup outcomes unverified.
Role-specific Catalog runs are correctly bounded as direct local-handler observations; they do not prove member/admin access controls, Ask/Act denial, or agent advertisement/binding.
